messages:
emily.s: Heads-up: OSV/Snyk just flagged two related issues affecting our services — grpc-go CVE-2026-1234 (server stream header parsing) and golang.org/x/oauth2/jwt CVE-2026-5678 (JWT claim verification bypass). net/http note: the Go stdlib advisory CVE-2026-9012 for HTTP/2 header handling might also matter for some internal clients. Impact: a few internal services that accept external requests and our inference router.

rafael.t: Thanks — do we have exact versions impacted? can we patch non-disruptively?

emily.s: grpc-go <= v1.53.0 impacted; oauth2/jwt <= v0.5.0 impacted; net/http is fixed in go1.21.4 and go1.20.12 (we run go1.20.6 in most services). Immediate plan: triage, make a minimal patch PR with pinned versions + tests, run full CI + canary. Need input on runtime compatibility (grpc and protobuf) and CI gating.

ci-bot: Automated scan results: https://osv.redwood-internal/reports/1840001234
- grpc.go: CVE-2026-1234 severity HIGH (exec path: header parse)
- oauth/jwt: CVE-2026-5678 severity HIGH (claim validation)
- stdlib/net/http: CVE-2026-9012 MEDIUM (HTTP/2 corner case)

jamal.k: Runtime note: our serving runtime links grpc-go and google.golang.org/protobuf v1.30.x. grpc-go v1.54+ requires protobuf >= v1.28 (we're at 1.27 in a few services). Upgrading grpc will require protobuf bump in some modules; that can be done in-place but watch generated pb.go diffs.

rafael.t: Suggested patch approach:
1) Create branch security/grpc-oauth-hotfix
2) Add explicit require pins in go.mod and update go.sum
3) For services using go1.20, plan to upgrade to go1.20.12 (minimal stdlib fix) via CI image bump
4) Run unit + e2e + smoke, then canary in staging (10% instances) for 48h
5) If OK, rollout to prod via staged deploys

Example go.mod snippet we'll include in the PR:

```
module github.com/redwood/service-router

go 1.20

require (
    google.golang.org/grpc v1.54.0
    golang.org/x/oauth2 v0.5.1
    google.golang.org/protobuf v1.28.0
)

// temporary replace for backport testing
replace google.golang.org/grpc => google.golang.org/grpc v1.54.0
```

emily.s: Also: do NOT use replace in long-term; only for quick cluster-wide rebuilds if CI is blocked. Prefer proper require + tidy.

mika.p: Audit/KMS notes: when we run canary, enable elevated audit logging for the canary instances (token events + RBAC changes). Also rotate the service KMS keys used by the router every 24h window? That might be heavy — at minimum log and tag requests for easier rollback investigation. Who can enable extra logs in staging?

rafael.t: I can flip the staging log level and enable request tagging. For KMS rotation: not in this sprint. We'll add an alert to the rollout checklist for key-rotation follow-up.

jamal.k: Testing checklist for runtime:
- build binaries with upgraded protobuf + grpc
- run pb.go regeneration and confirm no behavioral changes
- unit tests + fuzz for header parsing
- integration interop tests with older clients (grpc v1.52) — ensure compat
- load test at 2x normal QPS during canary

emily.s: Risk scoring: grpc CVE = HIGH (remote header parse), oauth JWT = HIGH (claims bypass), net/http = MEDIUM. Prioritize grpc > oauth > stdlib. Target: PR raised within 4 hours, canary within 48 hours.

ci-bot: Created issue #SE-2026-77 and linked PR template: https://git.internal/redwood/SE-2026-77

rafael.t: I'll create the PR and assign reviewers @jamal.k @emily.s. Will include a clear rollback plan (pin old versions + deploy). Also will add a smoke test that rejects malformed header sequences.

mika.p: I'll own staging canary ops and watch audit logs. Ping me when PR is merged.

emily.s: Action items:
- rafael.t -> open PR with pinned versions and CI jobs (ETA 4h)
- jamal.k -> run pb regen and run header fuzzing tests (ETA 1 day)
- mika.p -> enable extra logs for staging canary (ETA immediate after PR merged)
- security -> draft external notice template in case of public exploit (I'll start)

rafael.t: Starting branch now. tagging thread for visibility :rotating_light:

emily.s: Thanks everyone. Keep updates here — if we see failing tests, post minimal reproducer and I'll prioritize hotpatch.
